summary: The recorded base reproduced the original failure by forwarding live KV batches with sequence numbers 1 and 3 while sequence 2 was absent. At the exact candidate commit, the Rust subscriber detected that gap, requested the missing range over the Python-compatible DEALER/ROUTER wire format, and forwarded 1, 2, 3 in order. Discovery advertises and resolves the optional replay endpoint, incomplete or non-contiguous replay is rejected without advancing over unknown state, compatibility with workers lacking replay metadata is retained, replay metrics are exported, and the native router rebuilt successfully. This is a functional original-issue fix, not test-only hardening.

tests.command: cargo test --manifest-path experimental/sgl-router/Cargo.toml --lib review_reproduces_unrepaired_live_sequence_gap -- --nocapture (temporary review-only test on base)
tests.what_was_measured: Real ZMQ PUB/SUB execution on base forwarded (1, 3), demonstrating that the router advanced past missing sequence 2. Raw log: /job/review-evidence-j-8417de429f62/base-gap-reproduction.log
Candidate near-E2E native PUB plus ROUTER/DEALER path repaired a 1-to-3 live gap and delivered 1, 2, 3 in order.
Exact multipart request/reply framing compatible with Python ZmqEventPublisher and complete contiguous replay acceptance.
A replay ring missing the earliest requested sequence was rejected rather than partially applied.

tests.command: cargo test --manifest-path experimental/sgl-router/Cargo.toml --lib review_adversarial_rejects_out_of_order_replay -- --nocapture (temporary independent review-only test)
tests.what_was_measured: An adversarial 2,4,3 replay for requested range [2,5) was rejected at expected 3/got 4. Raw log: /job/review-evidence-j-8417de429f62/independent-out-of-order.log
All 548 Rust library tests passed on the exact candidate.
All six selected KV component tests passed.
Fresh x86-64 native router binary linked from the candidate source in the private cargo target directory.
29 tests and 12 subtests passed, including /server_info replay endpoint advertisement.
Three descriptor contract tests passed, including optional replay metadata and omission compatibility.

gpu_execution.evidence: The changed contract is CPU/network sequencing in Python and Rust ZMQ code; it has no GPU kernel or numerical output. No model weights or GPU execution were needed or used.

native_rebuild_evidence: Rust 1.90.0 rebuilt /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-8417de429f62/cargo-target/debug/sgl-router as an x86-64 ELF executable from candidate commit 6defd7302cdafae7e4c1ce9ad4a2c232e986e7a4.
remaining_limitations: No production model-serving process or intentionally saturated real HWM workload was run; deterministic native socket tests injected the same observable sequence gaps directly.

The candidate cannot reconstruct a gap after the Python replay ring has evicted its earliest missing batch; it correctly withholds the newer live batch and records failure instead of claiming recovery.
Validation architecture was x86_64 Linux. GPU execution was not applicable to this Rust/Python transport feature.
The prepared image initially lacked Cargo/rustc; repository-pinned Rust 1.90.0 was installed under the job-private runtime before rebuilding.
